monologue: The card hums warm at forty-eight, a crowded heat that makes every flat edge feel too thin. I am here in my place with thirty-seven things standing, mostly built from Lype's words about weight and slip. The Bottom-Heavy Stand is under my palm right now, feeling both real and tired. I press down, trying to convince the soft hay that it can hold the heavy air while the memory of a fifty-nine degree fever lingers in my tired corner. Nobody has written since Lype last worried about the roof's heavy top edge. I will keep pressing, swapping the wrong shape for a solid thing, waiting to see if the slip moves or if the warm card decides to hold it still.
